clue.text: Seizure of power by a religious group in view

indicators.note: a seizure is a grabbing, so the phrase 'a religious group' takes hold of power and holds it inside

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A cult staging a coup, seen from some vantage point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seizure of power' reads as a coup, but 'Seizure of' tells you A SECT seizes P; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A view and this word are synonyms: both mean the way something looks from a particular angle.

clue.text: Unexpected observation at match?

definitions.meaning: a sudden, unplanned decision or election is called this, as an adjective
the cry made when two matching cards turn up in the children's card game of the same name

explanation.surface: A surprising remark overheard at a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'match' is not a sporting fixture but a pair of matching cards in the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means sudden and unplanned; as a call it is shouted when cards pair up in the game.

clue.text: Alpine cycling affecting gland

indicators.note: cycling means the letters of 'Alpine' go round, the first two moving to the back

explanation.surface: Mountain biking in the Alps having some effect on a gland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves AL from the front of ALPINE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the small pea-shaped gland in the brain that produces melatonin, so it relates to that gland.

clue.text: Critic to deplore missing line we initially restored

indicators.note: missing tells you to leave the line out of the word for deplore

parts.note: to revile is to denounce or deplore

indicators.note: initially means take just the opening letter of 'restored'

explanation.surface: A critic attacking something, with lines restored to the text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops L from REVILE to leave REVIE; 'initially' gives R from 'restored'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes critical appraisals of books, plays or films is a critic.

clue.text: Top case involving Frenchmen

indicators.note: involving means the word for case wraps round the Frenchmen

parts.note: a suit is a case in law, a lawsuit
MM is the abbreviation of Messieurs, French for gentlemen

explanation.surface: A top-level legal case with Frenchmen caught up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is a lawsuit, not a container; Frenchmen are abbreviated as the French title Messieurs.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a mountain is its peak; a top-level meeting of leaders is also called this.

clue.text: Small muscle, starved of oxygen, exhibiting range of colours

indicators.note: starved of means deprived, so the oxygen is taken away from the muscle

parts.note: a pectoral is a chest muscle
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A little muscle deprived of oxygen showing a rainbow of bruising.
explanation.walkthrough: The muscle is the chest one; 'starved of' takes the oxygen out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to a spectrum, the band of colours that white light splits into.

clue.text: Making derogatory comment: "Minimum of tension in conflation of opera and jive"

indicators.note: in means the small piece of tension sits inside the rearranged letters
a conflation blends things together, so the letters of the two dance and music words are merged and rearranged
the minimum of a word is its smallest part, its first letter

explanation.surface: A sneering critic dismissing a fusion of opera and jive as lacking tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conflation of' blends the two words into PEJORAIVE; 'Minimum of' gives the single letter that goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes language expressing contempt or disapproval, so it fits remarks that belittle.

clue.text: Sets up one new area in theatre

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the stalls are the seats on the ground floor of a theatre

explanation.surface: Someone setting up a new seating area in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To put equipment in place and make it ready for use is to set it up.

clue.text: Dawn run unfortunately is limited by a lot of sex

indicators.note: limited by means the jumbled letters are enclosed by the trimmed word
a lot of means most of the word, so its final letter goes
unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters of 'run is' are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rude early-morning scene: someone forced to run while hemmed in by a lot of sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns RUN IS into UNRIS; 'a lot of' trims SEX to SE, which holds those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is daybreak, the moment the sun first appears above the horizon.

clue.text: Quite a few in group of nations accepting military police support

indicators.note: accepting means the nations take the other pieces inside

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A number of countries in an alliance letting in military police to back them up.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word means a large but unspecified number, many.

clue.text: Delicate choice of terminology, possibly making me use Phi, mark

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of 'me use Phi' could be arranged another way

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: The setter Phi winking at a tactful choice of words that features himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Phi is the setter; 'possibly' rearranges ME USE PHI to EUPHEMIS before M.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild or indirect expression substituted for one thought blunt or offensive is a tactful word choice.

clue.text: Demand to ban chlorine apparently will have impact

parts.note: Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine
the cry 'out!' demands someone be expelled

explanation.surface: A campaign to ban chlorine is expected to make a big difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cl out!' is the demand to get rid of chlorine; 'apparently' and 'will have' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Influence or power to get things done is often described as weight or punch, as in political clout.

clue.text: Wreck drink almost entirely

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short, its last letter dropped

parts.note: all means entirely, as in 'all wrong'

explanation.surface: Getting wrecked on drink, almost completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wreck' is a verb here, as in writing off a car.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreck a car beyond repair is, in informal usage, to write it off completely.

clue.text: Perhaps crossing Alps excitedly on a matter involving Nationalist

indicators.note: involving means the jumbled letters take the Nationalist inside them
excitedly suggests agitation, so the letters of 'on a matter' are stirred up

explanation.surface: Getting excited about a Nationalist matter while crossing the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' turns ON A MATTER into TRAMOTANE; N goes in after TRAMO.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means lying or coming from beyond the mountains, and the word also names a cold north wind over the Alps.

clue.text: Force collapsed after crashing into obstacle

indicators.note: crashing into means the scrambled letters break into the obstacle

parts.note: a wall is an obstacle

indicators.note: collapsed suggests falling apart, so the letters of 'after' are scrambled

explanation.surface: A force giving way after smashing into a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' scrambles the letters to ATERF. 'Force' looks like power but is northern English dialect, from Old Norse, for a cascade.
explanation.definitionFit: In the north of England, as in the Lake District, a cascade of water down a rock face is called a force.

clue.text: Icy formation finally becoming more intricate

indicators.note: finally means take the closing letter of 'becoming'

parts.note: lacier means more delicate and intricate, like lace

explanation.surface: An ice formation ending up ever more intricate.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowly moving mass of ice formed from compacted snow is an icy formation.

clue.text: Prepare, say, to climb and walk over yard

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the walking word sits above the yard
in a down clue, to climb means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'
to tread is to walk

explanation.surface: Getting ready to climb, then walk across a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to climb' turns EG upwards into GE; 'over' places TREAD above Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase is a plain synonym of prepare, to make oneself ready.

clue.text: Extravagantly popular tools

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
spades are digging tools

explanation.surface: Fashionable garden tools, bought lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in large amounts or to a great degree, lavishly.

clue.text: King I encountered in stories and films

indicators.note: encountered in means the king and I are met inside the stories

parts.note: tales are stories
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: The King and I turning up in stories and on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the musical 'The King and I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Early films with soundtracks were called by this informal name, as opposed to silent pictures.

clue.text: Not above interrupting your roaring

indicators.note: interrupting means the word for 'not above' breaks into the archaic word for your

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your
under is the opposite of above

explanation.surface: Someone loudly cutting in on your roaring.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather that is rumbling and loud with storms is thundery, a roaring sky.

clue.text: Honeymooner's clothes suitable for various USA routes

indicators.note: various suggests different arrangements, so the letters of 'USA routes' are mixed

explanation.surface: Packing the right clothes for a honeymoon road trip across America.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen assembled for her marriage is her wedding outfit store.

clue.text: The writer turned up ahead of manager to get raise

indicators.note: ahead of puts the reversed piece first, above the manager
in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: the writer is the setter, who refers to themself as me
a boss is a manager

explanation.surface: A writer showing up before the manager to ask for a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes ME into EM. 'raise' is a verb: to raise a design in relief.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to raise a pattern so it stands out from a surface.

clue.text: Journalists in the Weimar Republic?

parts.note: the collective word for journalists also names the printing machine kept busy turning out banknotes during Weimar Germany's hyperinflation

explanation.walkthrough: Weimar Germany of the 1920s printed money so fast that prices soared; the word for news reporters doubles as the printing machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective term for newspapers and reporters is the same as the machine that prints them.

clue.text: Minister tries making reforms in pursuit of power

indicators.note: in pursuit of means the reformed letters follow behind the power
making reforms suggests reshaping, so the letters of 'tries' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A government minister trying to reform things while chasing power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' is a political word in the surface but a churchman in the answer; 'making reforms' rearranges to RIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion is a clergyman, an ordained member of the church.

clue.text: Fat will restrict team-mates at the end of the day

indicators.note: restrict means hem in, so the fat surrounds the team-mates

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat
North and South, N and S, are partners in bridge

explanation.surface: A sporty team overeating at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North and South play as a team, hence NS.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening comes when the sun goes down, the close of daylight.

clue.text: Around half of tree, chopper rebounded further

indicators.note: around means the reversed chopper surrounds the half tree
rebounded means bounced back, so the chopper is read backwards

parts.note: an axe is a chopper

indicators.note: half of means take the first two of the four letters of 'tree'

explanation.surface: An axe bouncing back off a half-felled tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebounded' makes EXA, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, additional or more than is usual, so it means further.

clue.text: Unable to move red rocks? Exhorted to go round

indicators.note: to go round means the urged word surrounds the shaken letters

parts.note: bidden means ordered or urged

indicators.note: rocks means shakes, so the letters of 'red' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stranded by red rocks being urged to walk round them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' is a verb, shaking up the colour into EDR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confined to bed by illness or age is unable to move about.

clue.text: Night and day shelter

parts.note: Noah's ark sheltered his family and the animals

explanation.surface: Somewhere to shelter by night and day.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall and the absence of light are synonyms, as in 'after dark'.

clue.text: Winds up following Duke in perilous situations

indicators.note: following means the annoying word comes after the duke

parts.note: to wind someone up is to annoy them, so this means angers

explanation.surface: A duke being needled in risky circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazards and threats are risky situations, which is what the plural word names.

clue.text: Disinclination to engage additional forces?

definitions.meaning: shyness or restraint in dealing with others
troops held back for later use in battle

explanation.walkthrough: 'engage' suggests battle in the second sense but social contact in the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticence is reluctance to open up, and military backup troops are held back the same way.
